title: .saasaloy/manifest.json — managed-file tracking
description: Records every file a module applied — copied source files and copied skill files — with the owning module and a content hash, so update/remove know exactly what to undo. Replaces in-file `// saasaloy:managed` markers (build spec §2.9 / §3.2). `saasaloy init` writes it first, with one entry per base template file under the reserved module name `base` (ADR 0032).

when.description: The descriptor `when` the entry was written under (#242). `remove X` reads it offline to also remove another module's entries whose `installed` names X.

testing.description: Ship only when testing.mode is `tests-after` or `tdd`. The one allowed value is `true`; leave the key out for an entry that ships in every mode.

installed.description: Ship only when every named module is installed. `remove` of a named module also removes the entry.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor validation.

managed.description: Project-relative file path → the module that owns it and a content hash. On update the tool re-hashes the file: match → safe overwrite; drift → route to AI-merge.

module.description: Name of the module that applied this file. `base` is reserved for the template `saasaloy init` rendered; it is never in saasaloy.json's `installed` list.

hash.description: sha256 hex digest of the file's content as written.

adopted.description: True when the hash is of bytes the tool found on disk rather than bytes it wrote — `saasaloy update` adopting a project that had no base record. Those bytes may carry hand edits, so `update` routes an adopted file to the merge plan instead of overwriting it. Cleared the first time the tool writes the file itself.

from.description: Module-relative POSIX source path this file was copied from (e.g. `files/lib/email.ts`). `update` uses it to fetch the same file at the old and new commit SHAs. Optional — entries written before this field shipped fall back to re-deriving the target from the module descriptor.

mergedWith.description: sha256 of the module's version a merge took in, set by `saasaloy update --resolved <path>`. The entry's `hash` is then of the merged bytes. While the module still ships that version `update` skips the file; once it moves, the file goes to the merge plan rather than being overwritten. Cleared the first time the tool writes the file itself.

links.description: Symlink map (source path → link path): a module's skill files live under .agents/skills/<name>/ and `add` points a .claude/skills/<name> symlink at them, recorded here so `remove` can undo both (ADR 0015).

removeWarnings.description: Installed module name to removal warnings copied from its descriptor. The remover reads this map offline.

pendingNotes.description: Update notes an applied `saasaloy update` showed and nobody has cleared yet (#298), in the order they were first shown. Each prints again in every later merge plan until `saasaloy update --done <id>` clears it, and `saasaloy remove <module>` drops the notes that module owns. The rendered body is stored, so the note repeats with no registry fetch. Optional: a manifest without it has no pending note.

id.description: The note id, `base/NNNN-<slug>` or `<module>/NNNN-<slug>`, derived from its path.

body.description: The note's Markdown after the frontmatter, as the merge plan rendered it.

mayApply.description: True when the run could not place the note, so the merge plan lists it under "Notes that may apply".

doneNotes.description: Update note ids `saasaloy update --done <id>` cleared (#298), sorted, once each. Selection skips every id listed here, so a note a later run selects again (an adopted base at the running CLI, a module with no merge base) never returns. `saasaloy remove <module>` drops the ids that module owns, so a re-add starts clean. Optional: a manifest without it has no done note.

patches.description: Structural config patches actually applied to disk, so `remove` can warn which files it can't clean up on its own (reversal is a follow-up issue). Deduped on re-apply (structural equality) so `--force` stays idempotent.

module.description: Name of the module that applied this patch.

file.description: Project-relative POSIX path of the file that was patched.

kind.description: Which codemod applied this patch. Must list exactly the kinds registry-item.schema.json accepts — the applier records here whatever a descriptor authored, so a kind missing from this enum makes the next `loadManifest` refuse a manifest the tool itself wrote (#98). `schema.test.ts` asserts the two enums and the `Patch` union agree.

patch.description: The op as authored (kind + payload + file), re-applicable at execute time.
